gap: No result ChatGPT got states that LinkdHOME (David Mead) ran the same 30-day test on both doorbells it showed and measured the eufy E340 well ahead of the SwitchBot Video Doorbell on every head-to-head figure: daytime chart legibility 6.7 m vs 2.3 m, battery run to dead 78 vs 47 days, human detection 76% vs 46%, and average live-view load 1.04 s vs 5.3 s.
standout_why: I compared against the cited smarthomeperfected.com picks page, which says it did no hands-on testing and only repeats listing specs (2K, 165°, 5,000 mAh, 4.3-inch). I also checked the top result, worthrated.com, which has no measured figures, attributes its numbers to Amazon listings and doesn't cover eufy or SwitchBot. The cited eufy bundle page gives only maker specs (8-inch screen, 4,050 mAh, 'All-Day Power'). None of these pages has a measured figure for either card.
decides: This backs the eufy E340 + E10 as the pick over the SwitchBot kit, unless budget decides. The SwitchBot doorbell and monitor may cost far less (store listings: $149.99 for the doorbell, $69.99 for an add-on monitor), but LinkdHOME measured it reading a chart at only about a third of the distance, missing 25% of night detections, dying in 47 days, and taking 5.9 s from ring to live view. A shopper who wants a screen that shows a clear face quickly should take the eufy. The SwitchBot is a budget choice with known weaknesses. One caveat: LinkdHOME tested the E340 without the E10 display (it used HomeBase 2 and an Echo Show), so the doorbell figures carry over but none measure the E10 screen itself.
